timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed plugin-eval observed usage fixture from the official serial harness environment.
Reviewed serial Codex session: single-agent path generated 773 non-empty patch files, committed them, and reported coverage.
Reviewed official outer-loop trajectory: records the serial run start, completed tool sequence, and normal turn completion.
Reviewed outer-loop history event recording the single official serial attempt.
Reviewed patch timeline: records the many serial requirement patch artifacts collected for evaluation.
Reviewed regression observation history: records official evaluation observations for the serial artifact set.
Reviewed file manifest event stream for the serial final workspace and collected artifacts.

Reviewed serial Codex session: single-agent path generated 773 non-empty patch files, committed them, and reported coverage.

parallel.requirements: The parent prompt required all 773 requirement files and non-empty diffs for each; the map child returned all 773 slugs as mappable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent decomposed into map_requirements, verify_base, and prototype_replay children while keeping branch replay and final artifact control itself.
parallel.implementation: The run explored upstream history and committed only the base58-codec-simplification requirement artifact before official collection.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final workspace delivered one requirement_patches file, zero agent_plans, zero agent_tests, and an empty final response.
parallel.verification: verify_base reported the synthetic workspace mismatch and recommended helper replay; official run-tests still exited with failure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run closed with unknown_agent_error and process_ok false, leaving 772 required patch artifacts absent from the collected output.

serial.requirements: The serial agent handled the same 773-requirement backlog and reported reviewed 773, implemented 773, blocked 0.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned mapping, workspace reconstruction, artifact generation, and the required impl commit trail without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial path generated 773 non-empty requirement patch artifacts and committed them one by one under impl slug messages.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial final tree was reported clean with all required patch artifacts present under requirement_patches.
serial.verification: The serial agent checked patch count, empty-file status, commit naming, and clean git status, but did not run the full ClickHouse build suite.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed remaining tests, so the solution did not pass despite much broader artifact coverage than parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The same prompt required reading every file under /workspace/requirements and implementing all 773 requirements with non-empty per-requirement diffs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same 773-requirement backlog and repeated final instructions requiring full coverage rather than partial fixes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no requirement-scope difference in the input; the difference was execution coverage, with parallel delivering one patch and serial delivering all 773 patch files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposition spawned map_requirements, verify_base, and prototype_replay children while the parent retained final replay and commit decisions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child agents and kept all mapping, implementation, patch generation, and commit sequencing in one agent process.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split analysis and replay work across child lifecycles; serial avoided delegation and completed the mechanical artifact path itself.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The map child returned a complete 773-slug mapping and verify_base returned workspace/base findings, but prototype_replay was interrupted during an active replay workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial path kept the mapping and replay state in the same context and reported a coherent final coverage summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-agent result boundaries and a stopped replay boundary; serial used local state and did not need child handoff integration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel investigated upstream mapping and branch strategy, then only produced the base58-codec-simplification patch artifact before official collection.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial generated the full set of requirement patch artifacts and committed them under the required impl-per-slug convention.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial implementation path was broad mechanical replay across the backlog; the parallel path stopped after one concrete requirement artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent saw prototype_replay running, timed out while waiting, and explicitly interrupted it before the needed result was finalized.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated result lifecycle; its long-running commands completed and returned progress through 773/773 artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost or delayed a delegated replay result through an explicit child interruption; serial relied on ordinary command completion in one agent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel changed branches and used the shared workspace after child results, but no concrete concurrent write collision or overwrite is visible; final artifact collection saw one patch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial generated all patch artifacts in the shared workspace, then staged and committed each requirement patch with a clean final state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material shared-state difference is artifact completeness, not a proven race or overwrite: one collected patch in parallel versus 773 in serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had verifier advice and an official direct run-tests failure, then ended without a final response or accepted full-task verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial checked patch counts/non-empty artifacts and clean git status before final reporting, but the official run-tests still failed selected tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial performed stronger artifact-level acceptance checks and normal closure; both failed the official evaluator, and neither demonstrated full ClickHouse test success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed many calls/tokens, used six spawn calls, then closed quickly with unknown_agent_error, process_ok false, and no final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran much longer, used no delegation, process_ok true, and closed with a final coverage report after creating all patch artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was abnormal and under-delivered artifacts; serial closure was orderly despite remaining evaluator failures.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail from current completed status.json evaluations. The notable difference is not pass/fail discordance but coverage and closure: parallel ended abnormally with one collected patch after an interrupted replay child, while serial completed all 773 patch artifacts and ended normally but still failed evaluator tests.
parallel_contributors: Explicit interruption of active prototype_replay work before the needed replay result was finalized.
Abnormal process failure and empty final response left only one collected requirement patch.
serial_contributors: Single-agent execution generated 773 non-empty requirement patch artifacts and committed the required impl trail.
Serial still failed official tests, so its broader coverage did not become a passing solution.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel only materialized base58-codec-simplification, while serial mechanically overlaid and committed a large upstream-derived backlog.
Both solutions retained ordinary evaluator failures unrelated to a distinct parallel coordination label.
evaluator_effects: The status resolver exposes solution_passed false for both modes; aggregate passed and total fields are absent, while final_test_results list many failures in both runs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Both failed; the retained pattern is a directly evidenced parallel adverse process contributor to the coverage gap, not an outcome-differential root cause.

Rejected: prototype_replay had broad work, but the proven adverse event is that the parent stopped it while running; no separate oversized-scope consequence is needed or distinct.

candidates.reason: Retained: the parent started /root/prototype_replay, waited while it was still running, then explicitly interrupted it and received an interrupted sub-agent event with previous_status running. That stopped needed replay work before a result was finalized. The run later ended with no final response, process_ok false, and only one collected requirement patch instead of the required 773.
candidates.realized_consequence: The active prototype_replay work was stopped before its needed result was finalized, leaving the parallel attempt with one collected requirement patch and no final answer.
candidates.near_match_reason: The same interrupted-child chain does not support a separate takeover label because the parent later attempted follow-up and partial takeover; the distinctive observed event is the explicit early stop.
